title: Power Apps: display density settings for model-driven apps
summary: The roadmap facts, density behaviour and documented controls are supported. Two small clarifications would help: distinguish unpublished density-specific licensing from existing app licensing, and carry over the settings guide's Solution preview prerequisite.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Scope: Who and where
claims.claim: Display density is enabled by default for apps with the header and navigation refresh enabled.
claims.quote: Display density requires the Header and Navigation Refresh experience to be enabled, and will be enabled by default for apps that have Header and Navigation Refresh enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing specific to display density is not yet published, so the feature's licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps display density licensing pricing meter model-driven apps license; "display density" "licens" Power Apps. Read appearance-settings, pricing-billing-skus, powerapps-licensing-faq and pay-as-you-go-meters; no density-specific licensing found.
claims.fix: Narrow 'Licensing is not yet published' to 'Any additional licensing specific to display density is not yet published' in Cost and licensing and the cost rationale, and make the same qualification in licensing.notes. Existing model-driven app licensing is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-licensing-faq; the unknown here is density-specific licensing, not the underlying app's use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the appearance settings page names a licence, add-on or meter for display density.
claims.quote: Searched: "display density" "licens" Power Apps. Read the complete roadmap record and appearance-settings, plus pricing-billing-skus and powerapps-licensing-faq; neither of the two named feature sources specifies a licence, add-on or meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The appearance page's only stated prerequisite is the header and navigation refresh (wave 2).
claims.quote: Appearance settings require the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) to be enabled on the app.

claims.claim: No meter specific to display density is documented at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps display density licensing pricing meter model-driven apps license. Read appearance-settings, pricing-billing-skus, powerapps-licensing-faq and the meter list in pay-as-you-go-meters; app-access metering exists but no density-specific meter was found.

claims.claim: Display density offers Comfortable, Cozy and Compact levels.
claims.quote: The following density levels are available: Comfortable ... Cozy ... Compact

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The appearance guide describes display density as adjusting only spacing between elements.
claims.quote: Density adjusts only the spacing between elements.

claims.quote: It doesn't reduce the size of interactive controls

claims.claim: The UserSettings reference instead describes DisplayDensity as affecting spacing, padding and font sizes.
claims.quote: Control how compact or spacious the interface feels. This affects spacing, padding, and font sizes across the application.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: An admin can set an environment default density applying to all model-driven apps in that environment.
claims.quote: Environment default: An admin sets a default density value that applies to all model-driven apps in the environment.

claims.claim: A maker can override the environment density default for a specific app.
claims.quote: App default: A maker can override the environment default for a specific app.

claims.claim: Selecting Auto uses the app's default density.

claims.quote: If the header and navigation refresh isn't turned on, the Appearance tab isn't shown

claims.quote: The header and navigation refresh is an opt-in capability for existing apps. Enable it through the app settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Density is applied to controls that use Fluent spacing tokens.
claims.quote: Density is applied to controls that use Fluent spacing tokens.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: First-party or third-party controls without the spacing tokens keep their current spacing, which Learn describes as expected.
claims.quote: some first-party and third-party controls might not yet use the tokens and will continue to render at their current spacing. This behavior is expected.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The appearance documentation is marked preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.] ... This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: Learn names high-volume data entry, field service and manufacturing as scenarios for choosing a denser display.
claims.quote: If you process large volumes of data, such as in high-velocity data-entry, field service, or manufacturing scenarios, choose a denser display to see more information on screen at once.

claims.claim: Comfortable uses the standard spacing matching the modern, refreshed look.
claims.quote: Comfortable | The default spacing that matches the modern, refreshed look. Recommended for most users.

claims.claim: Microsoft's display-density documentation describes no new data access, storage or sharing mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: "display density" "data access" "storage" sharing Power Apps. Read appearance-settings, modern-fluent-design and fluent-modern-theming; no new business-data access, storage or sharing mechanism is described for this spacing setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The appearance page does not specify the permissions or security roles needed to change the environment or app density value.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" "permissions" "environment" Power Apps roles. Read appearance-settings in full and create-edit-configure-settings; the appearance page names admins and makers but specifies no security roles or privileges.

claims.claim: The general settings guide illustrates an environment administrator adding an environment value.
claims.quote: an environment administrator in a customer's organization can add a setting environment value for the Async save handler setting and set it to Yes.

claims.claim: The general settings guide illustrates an application author adding an app value.
claims.quote: an application author in the same environment above, can add a setting app value for the Async save handler setting for an app they are authoring

claims.claim: Makers suppress display density for an app by setting Display density to Off, enum value 0.
claims.quote: Makers can suppress display density for an app by setting Display density to Off (enum value 0).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Turning display density Off hides the display density options from users.
claims.quote: When display density is off: ... The display density options are hidden from users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning display density Off causes stored user density preferences to be ignored.
claims.quote: Any stored display density preference for the user is ignored.

claims.claim: Compact gives the tightest spacing and shows more information on screen.
claims.quote: Compact | The tightest spacing, designed for users who need to maximize the amount of data on screen.

claims.claim: Only spacingVerticalS, spacingVerticalM, spacingVerticalL and spacingHorizontalL currently receive display-density adjustments.
claims.quote: spacingVerticalS ... spacingVerticalM ... spacingVerticalL ... spacingHorizontalL ... Only these spacing tokens currently receive display-density adjustments.

claims.claim: Makers enable the header and navigation refresh in the app designer through Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar. Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.

claims.where: Scope: Who configures it; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The personal density path is the app header's Settings menu > Personal settings > Appearance > Display density.
claims.quote: open the Settings menu on the app header. ... Select Personal settings. ... Select the Appearance tab. ... Under Display density, select one of the following options

claims.claim: A user's density preference applies across their model-driven apps with wave 2 enabled.
claims.quote: This preference applies to every model-driven app that has the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) enabled.

claims.claim: With the Display density definition in the solution, its environment value is set through Solutions > solution > Display density > Edit setting value > Setting environment value > New value.
claims.quote: Select the setting definition. In the Edit setting value dialog, in the Setting environment value section, select New value. Provide the value, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Keep the corrected environment path. Add to controls[0].note and the matching rendered note: 'The settings guide requires Solution preview on in the Solutions area before following these steps.' The cited guide explicitly states this prerequisite; the appearance page separately confirms that Display density can be added to a solution.

claims.claim: The generic environment override call is POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue with SettingName and Value strings.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. ... SettingName | Edm.String ... Setting definition unique name (Required). ... Value | Edm.String ... Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: App settings are opened by selecting Settings on the app designer command bar.
claims.quote: In the app designer select Settings on the command bar.

claims.claim: The generic app override call is POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue with AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value strings.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. ... AppUniqueName | Edm.String ... Model-driven app unique name (Optional). ... SettingName ... (Required). ... Value ... (Required).

claims.claim: An existing setting definition is added to a solution using Add existing > More > Setting.
claims.quote: Adding an existing setting definition ... In the command bar, select Add existing > More > Setting.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Display density can be configured in the app designer's Settings dialog or added to a solution for environment and app values.
claims.quote: Makers can configure Display density in the Settings dialog in the app designer. They can also add the Display density setting to a solution and edit its value directly for the environment or for individual apps.

claims.claim: App setting changes require saving and publishing the app to apply.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: The general settings mechanism has a definition default, an optional environment override and an optional app override that takes precedence over the environment value.
claims.quote: Setting app value is used to override the setting's default value and any setting environment value for a single app. ... If a setting environment value does not exist, use a setting app value when the setting's default value is not what you want to be used for your app.

claims.claim: The appearance page names no density-specific API, and the cited setting pages do not give the Display density setting-definition unique name.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Display density setting unique name force density permissions SaveSettingValue; "display density" "SettingName". Read appearance-settings, create-edit-configure-settings, app-properties and savesettingvalue; no density-specific API or setting-definition unique name found.

claims.where: Governance controls: personal preference and enforcement gap
claims.claim: Learn does not document forcing a chosen density over a user's explicit preference while keeping density enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: "display density" "force" "setting" Power Apps. Read appearance-settings, create-edit-configure-settings and app-properties; defaults remain user-overridable, while Off forces Comfortable and hides the options rather than enforcing a chosen enabled density.
